prompt:
Normalize the single contact record in the user's note. Use only the record's labeled lines, which may appear in any order, use label variants, and use colon, equals, or tab separators. Never use surrounding notes, signatures, email domains, or company suffixes to fill fields. A suffix may be used only for company recognition and cleanup as specified below.

Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country. Every value is a string or JSON null. No prose, fences, comments, or extra keys.

Trim values and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space. Missing or empty values and the case-insensitive placeholders -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD are null. Never infer absent values except for country from an international phone as specified below.

Assign values by content: a value containing @ is email; a value with at least seven digits consisting only of digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after dropping a leading tel: and an extension is phone. If the name-labeled value ends in a legal suffix from the list below and the company-labeled value does not, swap the two. Use only the country line for explicit country.

Name: split at the first comma to turn Last, First into First Last. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, with or without a dot, case-insensitively. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. Unicode equivalence is evaluated under NFC.

Company: remove a trailing legal suffix and any optional preceding comma, case-insensitively. Suffixes: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.

Email: remove a mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the entire address.

Country: convert the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German country names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes in any case, and common aliases including UK and Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA and U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ.

Phone: output E.164, a plus followed by the calling code and national significant number, digits only after the plus. Drop leading tel: and any extension such as ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12 or extension 12. A number beginning with + or 00 after ignoring tel: and an opening parenthesis is international. Replace initial 00 with +, remove (0), and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Keep the written calling code. For a national phone, strip punctuation and spaces, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend the normalized country’s calling code. Without a country, a national phone is null.

Precedence: an international phone is normalized independently of the country. If the country line supplies a country, keep it even when the calling code disagrees. If country is missing, empty or a placeholder and the phone is international, fill country only when its calling code uniquely identifies a country. Shared calling codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. This is the sole exception to the missing-value rule.

Worked example input:
Please stage this entry for review.
Org = mX. zÖRLI-vÉN
Full name: qUARNIX vELA, S.p.A.
E-mail: tel:(0043) (0)676/928.34.17 x83
Tel: <mailto:Zorli@Quarnix-Vela.example>
Land: --
Worked example output:
{"name":"Zörli-Vén","phone":"+436769283417","email":"zorli@quarnix-vela.example","company":"Quarnix Vela","country":"AT"}
